mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Mercedes G Class G 63 AMG engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mercedes G Class G 63 AMG engine replacement typically costs between £6,995 and £15,000 depending on engine code, condition type, and whether fitting is included. M157 units (2012-2018) range from £6,995 to £12,000, while M177 units (2018-present) range from £8,500 to £15,000. Rebuilt M157 (G 63 AMG 2012-2018): £6,995-£12,000 supply only. Rebuilt M177 (G 63 AMG 2018-present): £8,500-£15,000 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £3,500-£7,000 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £1,000-£1,800 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M157 turbo actuator failure in a G 63 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M157's electronic turbo actuator typically fails between 45,000-70,000 miles, with several warning signs. Sudden loss of power and acceleration. Check engine light illuminated. Limp mode activation. Fault code P0244 (Turbo Wastegate Actuator 'A' Range/Performance). Rattling or clicking noise from the turbo area.

mainEntity.name: Is the M177 engine in the G 63 AMG reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M177 is generally regarded as a reliable engine when properly maintained. However, it has several well-documented issues that owners should be aware of. Oil separator failure leading to rear main seal leaks. Intercooler leaks causing coolant loss and misfires. Excessive oil consumption. Timing chain stretch on some examples. Regular maintenance with 0W-40 oil and 5,000-7,000 mile intervals is critical.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my G 63 AMG engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., turbo actuator on M157, oil separator on M177, timing chain tensioner). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic turbo failure. M157 turbo actuator replacement: £600-£950 - excellent value if caught early. M177 oil separator replacement: £500-£800 - preventative if caught early. Full M157 rebuild: £6,995-£12,000 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Full M177 rebuild: £8,500-£15,000 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Given G 63 AMG values (£35,000-£180,000+), a rebuilt engine is typically excellent value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my G 63 AMG has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. G 63 AMG (2012-2018): M157.984 (5.5L twin-turbo V8). G 63 AMG (2018-present): M177.980 (4.0L twin-turbo V8). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used G 63 AMG engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a G 63 AMG. The complex 4MATIC system, twin-turbo plumbing, gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. 4MATIC transfer case alignment requires specialist knowledge. Twin-turbo system requires precise reassembly. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation needed. Specialist supply & fit costs £1,000-£1,800 - worth every penny for an AMG.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG relies on two of AMG's most celebrated twin-turbo V8s - the M157 and M177. While both are engineering masterpieces, they have developed well-documented reputations for specific, predictable failures. Turbo actuator failure on the M157 and oil separator failure on the M177 dominate replacement demand, while timing chain wear and oil consumption affect both families. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common G 63 AMG engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M157 Turbo Actuator Failure - Why the G 63 AMG Loses Power and Enters Limp Mode
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG (M157.984, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: The electronic turbo actuator (A1570940001) suffers internal gear and sensor degradation, causing the wastegate to stop responding - typically triggering limp mode and a check engine light. The high boost pressure and extreme heat generated by the twin turbos put significant stress on the actuator components.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty turbo actuator, recalibrate wastegate position, road test
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-70k miles; viable if turbo core is healthy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both actuators (twin turbo), inspect turbo cores, new gaskets
Supply & fit rebuilt M157 with upgraded actuators, new turbos if required
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; for catastrophic turbo debris ingestion

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 63 AMG (2012-2018) is worth £35,000-£80,000 depending on condition and mileage - the full replacement cost of £6,995-£12,000 is modest relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine excellent value. For vehicles worth under £25,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: On an AMG G 63 worth £35,000-£80,000, specialist actuator replacement at £600-£950 is the obvious first step. Dealer pricing is inflated for this repair. However, if the failure has caused turbo debris to enter the engine (metal particles in oil), you must go straight to full engine replacement - ignoring this risks complete bottom end failure within 1,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M157 Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG engine prices

problems.group: M177 Oil Separator & Rear Main Seal Failure
problems.h4: M177 Oil Separator & Rear Main Seal Failure - Why the New G 63 AMG Leaks Oil
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG (M177.980, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: The oil separator system can fail, creating excessive crankcase pressure or vacuum that damages the rear main seal. This leads to oil leaks that can cost thousands to repair and may require weeks in the workshop. Proper crankcase pressure balance is critical to the long-term health of the M177 engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil separator, inspect breather system, reset adaptations

repairOptions.tier: Major - Rear Main Seal & Oil Separator
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace rear main seal, oil separator, transmission removal required
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles; if oil leak is already present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M177 with upgraded oil separator, new seals
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W464 G 63 AMG (2018-present) is worth £60,000-£180,000+ - the full replacement cost of £8,500-£15,000 is small relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine excellent value for preservation.
problems.recommendation: The oil separator failure on the M177 is one of the most expensive common repairs. If you notice oil spots under your G 63 AMG or a burning oil smell, have the oil separator and rear main seal inspected immediately. Ignoring this can lead to catastrophic engine failure. Specialist repair at £1,500-£2,200 is significantly better value than dealer pricing.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M177 Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: M157 / M177 Timing Chain Wear - Why AMG G Class Engines Rattle on Start-Up
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG (M157.984, 2012-2018; M177.980, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: On early M157 engines (2011-2012), oil drainage from the cylinder head on start-up causes brief oil starvation of the timing chain tensioner, leading to chain stretch. Later M157 engines (2013+) received revised tensioners and check valves. The M177 can also suffer from timing chain stretch, with a rattling noise at startup being the primary symptom.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner, install check valve (M157), oil change
Replace all timing chains, tensioners, guides, sprockets
Supply & fit rebuilt M157/M177 with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required if chain has jumped

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 63 AMG worth £35,000-£180,000+, the timing chain repair at £450-£3,500 is justifiable. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: Early M157 G 63 AMG owners (2012 models) should have the timing chain tensioner and check valve inspected as a priority - the updated components from 2013 onwards address the oil drainage issue. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start that lasts more than 2 seconds, book a specialist inspection immediately. Ignoring timing chain issues on an AMG V8 can result in complete engine destruction.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M157 or M177 Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: M177 Intercooler Leaks - Why the New G 63 AMG Loses Coolant and Misfires
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 63 AMG (M177.980, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: The engine-mounted water-to-air intercoolers on the M177 can develop internal leaks, leading to coolant loss, misfires, and even catastrophic engine damage. This is a critical failure point that requires immediate attention.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both intercoolers, new coolant, system bleed, pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-80k miles; essential if coolant loss detected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M177 with new intercoolers, upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required if coolant has entered cylinders

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 63 AMG worth £60,000-£180,000+, the intercooler replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is essential maintenance. Ignoring it risks catastrophic engine damage.
problems.recommendation: The M177 intercooler leak is one of the most critical issues affecting the current G 63 AMG. If you notice coolant loss without an external leak, have the intercoolers inspected immediately. Specialist replacement is significantly cheaper than dealer pricing and far less expensive than a full engine rebuild.
